title: [recoverability] The controllers' drill, BUNDLE->X: restore-drill --only controllers also restores the sources from the newest bundle chain and checks X, the newest commit of each controller's history the backup holds, extracts from the mirror as from the live source; the lag said, never a failure; no commit held fails
prompt:
Spawn, objective 199 [recoverability], after 198 (the owner's order of 2026-11-14 18:43: restores passed must read 6 of 6, guardrail U1; drill 2 of the owner's four; the lead's split of 2026-11-15: 198 = LIVE, 199 = BUNDLE->X): the controllers' drill, BUNDLE->X. What each mission's live system runs from can be rebuilt from the off-site bundle.

198 checks each live controller against its commit in the live source. Nothing yet checks that the backup can give that tree back: 186 restores the mission repositories, and 198 never opens the bundle.

Base: 198, on live main b92d1289 (the throwaway below sits on 198's candidate 39c49370, on 186's candidate 00689e69; main's restore_drill.rs is the fleet's own 186).

Read first:
- crates/spawn-cli/src/backup/restore_drill/controllers.rs (198): named, drill_tree, the record;
- crates/spawn-cli/src/backup/restore_drill.rs: fetch_bundle and fetch_missions (186's pipe: gpg into tar -t, then tar -x of manifest.json and repos/*), restore_repo, chain_of.

What changes:
(1) `spawn backup restore-drill --only controllers` also restores the sources:
   - It fetches and unpacks the newest bundle chain as `--only missions` does: decrypted in a pipe, only manifest.json and repos/*, never a transcript; each controller's source restored from it as 186 restores a mission's repository.
   - HELD, per controller, for its current tree and its previous one (when there): X, the first commit of `git rev-list --topo-order <commit>` in the live source that the restored mirror holds; `git archive X` from the mirror equals `git archive X` from the live source, both extracted into scratch and compared as 198 compares (path, executable bit, sha256, symlink target). The lag from X to the live commit (lag_commits, lag_hours by committer time) is recorded and is never a failure: deploys are several a day and bundles one (bundle freshness is the backup line's own figure).
   - What HELD can prove, said plainly: the same commit id pins the same tree, and objects that pass fsck give the same archive, so HELD adds that X extracts whole from the off-site copy into a usable tree. No black box reaches a HELD difference; 198's unit test covers the tree compare (as 186 says of fsck --full).
   - A controller fails also when its HELD trees differ, or when the mirror holds no commit of its history.
   - Each record names the bundle (bundle, bundle_event_id), and current and prev gain held {commit, lag_commits, lag_hours, ok, files, differing [first 20]} | null. A run that cannot restore records one record with the drill fields alone, and exits 1 (2 only when that record is refused, as for every drill record).
(2) The owner's part: the unit's description and deploy/backup/README.md say the backup half; rsi/scenarios/199.sh (new). 198.sh stays as it is and passes.

What stays as it is: 198's LIVE check and record fields; the combined drill and --only missions; the schema (198 already takes held inside current and prev); the bundle; deploy/controller.sh; every controller and source (read only).
